clause.noServer: We run no server, and no copy of your lists exists anywhere we control.
clause.gateway: The app itself is delivered by a public web service (a gateway), which sees that you loaded it.
clause.relay: Relay nodes introduce devices to each other and may keep a copy of a list so another device can collect it later.
clause.sharedList: The list behind the share code is open: anyone who has its three Spanish words can read it and write to it. Treat the words as a way to meet, not as a password.
clause.privateList: A list you create yourself decides who may write to it - you, and anyone you let in. It does not decide who may read it.
clause.readingIsOpen: Todos and lists are not encrypted. Anyone who has a list’s address can read everything in it, including the relay that stores it. Do not put anything private in a todo.
clause.identityPasskey: Your passkey identifies you to the other devices. Nobody else can write as you.
clause.identityAnonymous: You are using a random identity that exists only in this browser. Close it and it is gone.
clause.delegation: You decide who may write to a list, and you can take a grant back later — unlike a key you handed out, because lists are not encrypted.
clause.storageMemory: “Keep in this browser” is unticked: nothing is written to this device, and this browser starts over when the page reloads.
clause.storagePersistent: “Keep in this browser” is ticked: your todos survive a reload. They sit unencrypted in this browser’s storage, and clearing it loses them.
clause.identityAnonymousKept: You are using a random identity that exists only in this browser. It keeps it until you clear the site data; nothing links it to you.
clause.amountsChain: An amount is encrypted on your device before it is sent, and it stays encrypted on a blockchain test network. Only you, the other party and the demo’s auditor can read it.
clause.amountsChainTechnical: An amount is encrypted in your browser (Zama TFHE) before it is sent, and it stays encrypted on the Sepolia testnet as a cUSDT balance under ERC-7984. Only you, the other party and the auditor named in the escrow contract can decrypt it.
clause.amountsPublic: Public on the blockchain are the sender, the recipient and the time of every payment — not the amount.
clause.amountsDemo: In this preview, budgets live only in this browser’s memory: nothing is encrypted and nothing reaches a blockchain.
clause.noBudgetWithoutPasskey: Without a passkey you cannot lock a budget: the passkey is what confirms a payment.
clause.gatewayTechnical: The app itself is delivered through a public IPFS gateway, which sees that you loaded it. Your own Kubo node, or the IPFS Companion extension, fetches it from the network instead.
clause.keys: This browser keeps the link to your passkey and the keys for signing and for reading amounts. The passkey itself never leaves your device.
clause.keysTechnical: This browser keeps your passkey’s public key and DID, and the keys for signing entries and for reading amounts. The passkey itself never leaves your authenticator.
clause.keysMemory: The keys for signing and for reading amounts live in this browser’s memory and are gone on reload. The passkey itself never leaves your device.
clause.keysMemoryTechnical: Your passkey’s public key and DID, the signing key and the read key live in this tab’s memory and are gone on reload. The passkey itself never leaves your authenticator.
clause.extensions: A browser extension with access to this page can read what it shows and what it keeps in this browser, keys included, and can change the page. Safest is a browser or browser profile of your own, without extensions. The passkey itself stays in your authenticator.
clause.extensionsTechnical: An extension with access to this page reads what it shows and keeps in the browser (DOM, localStorage, IndexedDB, the OrbitDB signing key included) and can inject code into it. The passkey’s private key stays in the authenticator.
clause.cookiesKept: No tracking cookies are used. Because this browser keeps things, it also keeps that you started here: next time the app opens without this dialog (with a passkey, after one tap).
clause.cookiesMemory: No tracking cookies are used, and not even your decision to start is saved: after a reload this dialog asks again.

technical: Passkey: a WebAuthn key with ES256 (P-256), stored discoverable and with the PRF extension. Your DID is a did:key of its public key (uncompressed, 0x04‖x‖y). The private key never leaves the authenticator.

OrbitDB signs your entries not with the passkey but with a secp256k1 key derived from the passkey's PRF output (HKDF-SHA256, separated by DID). So one passkey yields one identity on every device; the passkey signs only the identity document.

Keystore: OrbitDB's KeyStore. With "in memory only" the signing key lives in this tab's memory and is gone on reload. With "keep in this browser" it lives in IndexedDB (the Level database ./orbitdb/identities) under private_<DID>, as the raw 32 bytes, unencrypted.

Account: EIP-7702. The address of a setup key (secp256k1, in memory only during setup) gets the code of Uniswap's Calibur v1.0.0 (0x000000009B1D0aF20D8C6d0A44e162d11F9b8f00); the passkey is registered there as an admin key of type WebAuthnP256. The setup key is then discarded, but stays the account's root key for good.

Payments are ERC-4337 user operations to EntryPoint v0.8. The passkey signs their EIP-712 hash; Calibur checks the signature on chain with webauthn-sol, through the P-256 precompile (RIP-7212, address 0x100), otherwise in Solidity. On chain user verification is not required; only the app requires it.

Gas is paid by a paymaster: Openfort runs bundler and paymaster for Sepolia and sponsors under a rule for that chain, asked through ERC-7677 (pm_getPaymasterStubData, pm_getPaymasterData). Your account holds no ETH; the browser holds only Openfort's public key pk_test_….

Budgets are cUSDT, a confidential token under ERC-7984 (Zama's cUSDTMock on Sepolia, 6 decimals). On chain amounts exist only as euint64 handles; the arithmetic runs on the ciphertexts in Zama's coprocessors.

Locking: your browser encrypts the amount with Zama's SDK (TFHE, WebAssembly) and gets the input proof through Zama's relayer. The escrow contract ConfidentialTodoEscrow (0x6Ee3Fa9d3aEdaAD189F5DeA9d859605c9D743429) takes it with FHE.fromExternal and moves it with confidentialTransferFrom.

Reading: a second secp256k1 key, the read key, kept only sealed (AES-GCM under a key derived from the passkey's PRF output): in localStorage with "keep in this browser", in this tab's memory with "in memory only". It is authorised for 24 hours for escrow and token through ACL.delegateForUserDecryption. It signs EIP-712 read requests; your browser assembles the plain value from shares of 13 KMS nodes, 9 of which are needed.

Public remain the sender, recipient and time of every transfer, the link between account and read key (the DelegatedForUserDecryption event) and every read request on Zama's gateway chain. The amounts are not.

forget.title: Should this browser forget you?
forget.goes: This deletes everything this browser keeps for you: your sign-in here, and its copy of your lists and of your account details. The app then starts as on a new device and asks for your passkey again.
forget.unsynced: An entry that has not reached another device or a relay yet is lost with it.

forget.staysLists: Your lists, on your other devices and wherever a relay kept a copy.
forget.staysAccount: Your account on Sepolia, with its balance. The same passkey opens it again.
forget.technical: Deleted: this origin’s localStorage and sessionStorage in full, and every IndexedDB database under level-js-orbitdb/ and level-js-simple-todo/ — the passkey credential and identity proofs, the lists’ logs and registry, the account record, and any key this browser kept. The language carries over in the address; the theme and this technical view do not. The next start finds the identity on the authenticator again, as a new device does.
